turns.question: Where are streaming responses implemented, and which public API methods route into the streaming implementation?
turns.text:
I'll investigate the openai-node repository structure using the GitHub API/CLI without cloning it locally.Good, found the core files. Let me examine the key implementation files.It does have content. Let me retry the grep properly.Now let's check responses.ts for the Responses API streaming, and completions.ts (legacy) plus images/threads/transcriptions.Now let's look at the responses.ts `create` and `stream` methods (lines ~90-230), and check `ResponseStream.ts` lib file, plus threads/runs (Assistants), transcriptions, and images.Now let's check the higher-level streaming helper classes (ChatCompletionStream, ResponseStream, AssistantStream, EventStream) and images/transcriptions/threads for streaming.I have enough evidence now. Let me also check `client.post`/`get` in core/resource.ts and confirm APIClient.request passes `stream` into APIResponseProps.I have all the evidence needed. Here's the summary.

## Streaming implementation

**Core SSE/streaming engine** — `src/core/streaming.ts` (re-exported for compat from the deprecated `src/streaming.ts`):
- `Stream<Item>` class — wraps an `AsyncIterable`, exposes `.tee()`, `.toReadableStream()`, `[Symbol.asyncIterator]`.
- `Stream.fromSSEResponse(response, controller, client, synthesizeEventData)` — the main factory; parses the raw `Response` body as Server-Sent Events, JSON-decodes each `data:` line, stops on `data: [DONE]`, throws `APIError` if a chunk carries an `error` field.
- `Stream.fromReadableStream()` — alternate factory for newline-delimited JSON streams (used by realtime/WS-style responses).
- `_iterSSEMessages()` / `iterSSEChunks()` / `SSEDecoder` — low-level SSE line/byte decoding.

**Wiring from HTTP layer to `Stream`** — `src/internal/parse.ts`, function `defaultParseResponse()`: when `props.options.stream` is true, it calls `Stream.fromSSEResponse(...)` (or a custom `props.options.__streamClass` if set) instead of doing normal JSON parsing. This is the single chokepoint through which every "streaming" request is converted into a `Stream` object. The `stream` and `__streamClass` fields are declared on `FinalRequestOptions` in `src/internal/request-options.ts:48,82`.

**Higher-level convenience stream wrappers** built on top of `Stream`, in `src/lib/`:
- `EventStream.ts` — base class providing `.on()/.once()/.emitted()/.done()/.abort()` event-emitter semantics over a stream.
- `ChatCompletionStream.ts` (+ `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts`) — accumulates `ChatCompletionChunk`s into a final `ChatCompletion`, drives tool-call loops.
- `responses/ResponseStream.ts` — same idea for the Responses API (`ResponseStreamEvent` → final `Response`).
- `AssistantStream.ts` — same idea for the Assistants API (`thread.*` SSE events).

## Public API methods that route into streaming

All of these set `stream: <bool>` (or call a `Stream`-producing helper) on the request options passed to `this._client.post/get(...)`, which `defaultParseResponse` turns into a `Stream`:

| Method | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `client.chat.completions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:74-79` | returns `APIPromise<Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>>` |
| `client.chat.completions.stream(...)` | same file, `:221-226` | returns `ChatCompletionStream` (calls `ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion`) |
| `client.chat.completions.runTools(...)` w/ `stream:true` | same file, `:190-216` | returns `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner` |
| `client.completions.create({stream:true})` (legacy Completions) | `src/resources/completions.ts:41` | `APIPromise<Stream<Completion>>` |
| `client.responses.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:110-115` | `APIPromise<Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.responses.retrieve(id, {stream:true})` | same file, `:156-161` | streaming retrieve of an in-progress response |
| `client.responses.stream(...)` | same file, `:201-206` | returns `ResponseStream` (`ResponseStream.createResponse`) |
| `client.images.edit({stream:true})` | `src/resources/images.ts:58` | `APIPromise<Stream<ImageEditStreamEvent>>` (partial-image streaming) |
| `client.images.generate({stream:true})` | `src/resources/images.ts:91` | `APIPromise<Stream<ImageGenStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.audio.transcriptions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/audio/transcriptions.ts:62` | `APIPromise<Stream<TranscriptionStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.beta.threads.createAndRun({stream:true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/threads.ts:160` | `APIPromise<Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.beta.threads.createAndRunStream(...)` | same file, `:182-183` | returns `AssistantStream` |
| (also, by the same pattern) `client.beta.threads.runs.create({stream:true})` / `.stream(...)` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts` | not directly opened, but imports `RunCreateParamsStreaming`, `RunStreamParams`, `AssistantStream` analogous to threads.ts |

## Not verified
- I did not open `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts` contents directly (only saw its imports referenced in threads.ts) — I'm inferring its `create`/`stream`/`submitToolOutputs` methods follow the identical pattern based on the imported types (`RunCreateParamsStreaming`, `RunStreamParams`, `RunSubmitToolOutputsStreamParams`), but did not read the method bodies to confirm.
- I did not inspect `src/resources/responses/ws.ts`/`ws-base.ts` (WebSocket-based responses) or the realtime/websocket streaming path at all — question was scoped to "streaming responses" (SSE) so I treated WS as out of scope, but it's a second, separate streaming mechanism I haven't verified.
- I did not check every one of the 159 files in `src/resources` for `stream:` usage — I greped/sampled the ones most likely to matter (chat, completions, responses, images, transcriptions, threads) plus confirmed via `grep -rn '__streamClass'` found none outside `parse.ts`/`request-options.ts`, meaning all current streaming resources use the plain `Stream` class rather than a custom subclass.
- Version/commit: read from the `main` branch via GitHub API on 2026-07-05; I did not pin to a specific commit SHA, so exact line numbers could shift with future commits.
